data.long_meaning: One who preserves the universe, Lord Vishnu, the preserver and sustainer of life. data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Lord Vithoba is a form of Vishnu, the preserver and sustainer of life. He is worshipped predominantly in the state of Maharashtra, India. The name Vithoba is derived from "Vishwa-Bhа" which means protector or ruler of the universe, reflecting Lord Vithoba's role as a guardian and sustainer of your world. This deity has a distinct cultural significance in Maharashtra and is the principal god of the Maratha people.
data.spiritual_significance: Lord Vithoba is a symbol of love, devotion, and compassion. He is known for his tender nature and is often depicted with his Consort Rukmini or Andhakarudh, signifying his love for humanity. In deeper spiritual terms, Lord Vithoba represents the innermost self within us, our inner light and our own strength and ability to preserve and sustain our own lives, both materially and spiritually. His name is a powerful reminder that we hold the power within ourselves to preserve and continue in our lives, no matter the challenges we face.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vithoba is a popular name for the Hindu deity, Vitthala or Vishnu, in the Maharashtra region. The name Vithoba is believed to represent a loving and playful aspect of the deity. It signifies a protector, a nurturer, and a playful companion, always staying close to his devotees through their trials and tribulations.
